commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

The legacy scanner rejected a 255-character plain token even though the
256-byte scratch has room for that token and its terminating NUL. Copy
the token through knownhost_copy_legacy_name() so that limit lives in
one place.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling: The stack overflow is the terminating NUL of a legacy known-hosts host token, and it is reachable only when these two edits are both present. The IPv6 commit copies that token through knownhost_copy_legacy_name(), which accepts a 255-byte name. Against the 256-byte scratch that commit still declares, the name and its NUL fit exactly, and a longer name is rejected, so that commit does not write past the array. The later tidy commit changes the scratch from 256 bytes to 255. Against the previous sizeof check (namelen >= sizeof(hostbuf) - 1), the longest accepted name is 254 bytes and still fits in 255 with its NUL, so the shrink does not overflow either. Either edit applied alone leaves libssh2_knownhost_readline() in-bounds on a 255-byte token: the helper writes the NUL at the last byte of the 256-byte array, and the smaller array is still guarded by the sizeof check, which rejects that token before the store. Together the helper allows namelen == 255 and stores dst[255] in the 255-byte scratch (knownhost.c knownhost_copy_legacy_name, reached from knownhost_line_legacy). The limit and the array live in different functions and were changed in different commits; each diff is consistent with the scratch or the check it was written against. A correct fix has to reconcile the two: the scratch must be at least KNOWNHOST_LEGACY_NAME_MAX + 1, or the helper's limit must stay below the scratch size the tidy commit left behind. Looking at only one diff shows a locally consistent change and does not show the out-of-bounds store.
